target_customer: Mobile apps, marketplaces and merchants that take card payments and face stolen card fraud
problem: Typing card numbers is slow and enables stolen card fraud. DyScan uses camera card scanning and deep learning to speed checkout and verify that the physical card is present.
business_model: B2B SDK and API, per use pricing likely, details not found

founders.name: Lena Evans
founders.background_notes: Named as CTO in a Crunchbase snippet and as a founder in the Launch HN post; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time on device card recognition with deep learning across card formats, plus fraud signals, inside a sub 1 MB SDK, is hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: SDK integration into checkout flows and PCI compliance create switching costs; the models are copyable by larger vision vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy found as of 2026; the company remains independent with a live site.

market_need_then: Stolen card fraud and checkout friction were costly for apps; the launch post argued few companies used card scanning against fraud. Early contracts with Rappi and Gametime were reported in a Crunchbase snippet.

branding.domain_note: Uses dyneti.com as of 2026; history not found.

identity.logo: Indigo and dark grey variants per site
identity.visual_style: Clean enterprise layout with customer logos and case studies

brand_strength.rationale: Clear product brand DyScan and enterprise case studies, but no press on the brand and a coined name.

outcome_analysis: Dyneti joined YC in Winter 2019 and sells DyScan card scanning and fraud checks. Its site in 2026 shows customers including PayPal, DoorDash and FlightHub and vendor reported results such as 97 percent of stolen card fraud blocked at DoorDash. It appears to be a durable niche enterprise company, though funding and revenue are not public.
notes: Unverified: aggregators give a seed in March 2019 of 2.15 million (Bouncewatch) or 2.2 million with Shasta Ventures and YC (Clera), while CB Insights shows 0.15 million in February 2019, probably the YC deal. No primary source, so no round is recorded. Competitor list empty: the dated search found the Launch HN post but nothing naming 2019 competitors. Customer results are vendor claims. No outcome news found in a search that mostly returned other companies.
